reviews.instructor: MAK, Kelvin PLAI, Tai Wai David

sections.content:
A meaningless course.
All accounting student must take this course.
The first lecture will be the course introduction and the faculty meeting
The second lecture will be the teaching of the writing of CV
The following four lectures will have guest speakers from different industries to to have a talk.
After each lecture, you can choose to write a personal reflection on what the guest speaker says within a week. You need to submit at least two but not more than three personal reflections.
sections.teaching: There is no teaching from Prof Mak and David.
sections.grading:
Assessment:
Two reflective journals, each for 35%, total 70 %
Attendance and class participation (6 marks X 5 times), total 30%

The attendance and class participation basically does not count much and everyone gets full mark for this. Reflective journals grade are based on 5-point scale. It will greatly determine your grade.
The mean of each personal reflection is roughly 3.5, depending on the mood of the TA
Grade is basically determine based on:
Reflection 1 score: 4.5 Reflection 2: 4.0 or above --- A+
4.0 4.0 --- A
4.0 3.5 --- A-
3.5 3.5 ---B+ ---Mean Course Grade
3.5 3.0 ---B
3.0 3.0 ---B-
sections.workload: Workload is not very huge as the course ends at the middle of the semester. You only need to submit two personal reflections.The reflection is above 400 words each. The key is to relate what the guest said to your personal experiences, and you learn something important.

sections.content: Members of the accounting profession are expected to demonstrate high professional standard. Thus, professionalism is important to your career success. Your professional training begins in the undergraduate study at university. The course aims to deepen students’ understanding of the accounting profession and facilitate their career planning. An emphasis is also placed on ethics and the development of professionalism.

sections.content: Throughout the program, you are required to attend all workshops and talks organised by the faculty every week. The faculty invited business leaders to come to lectures to give you some insights on accounting industry and your career path, examples of guests were EY audit partner, CPA Australia representative, mediator, etc.
sections.grading: Not yet released, but only 1 credit, doesn't really affect your overall CGA lol
sections.workload:
Attendance is taken every class, so not recommended to skip lessons though there is one quota for you to skip without deducting your participation point.
Asking guests questions help you gain participation point.
You need to submit a reflective paper for at least 2 talks, max 3 talks, before the next week class began.
